executive_summary: On 2026-11-15, the SOC observed a series of anomalous ICMP packets originating from external IP 203.0.113.45 targeting internal host 10.0.5.23. The traffic exhibited unusually large payloads and repeated ping requests, indicative of an ICMP tunneling attempt used to establish a covert command‑and‑control channel and exfiltrate data.

attack_timeline.description: External actor sent crafted ICMP Echo Request with oversized payload to internal host, bypassing firewall rules that allowed ICMP.
Internal host responded, establishing a bidirectional ICMP tunnel used for command and control.
Malware encoded stolen data into subsequent ICMP Echo Replies, sending them to attacker IP.
Attacker ceased traffic after exfiltration, leaving minimal forensic traces.

mitre_attack.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Command and Control Channel

detection_gaps: Existing signatures only flag generic ICMP ping; they do not inspect payload size, content patterns, or frequency, allowing the tunneling channel to remain undetected.
recommended_snort_rules: alert icmp (msg:"MALWARE-ICMP Large Packet", icmp_type:8, dsize:>1400, sid:1000001, rev:1);
alert icmp (msg:"MALWARE-ICMP Ping Sweep", flow:to_server,established, icmp_type:8, threshold:type limit, track by_src, count 5, seconds 60, sid:1000002, rev:1);

alert icmp (msg:"MALWARE-ICMP Tunneling Detected", icmp_type:8, content:"|00 00 00 00|", offset:0, depth:4, nocase, fast_pattern, isdataat:64,relative, pcre:"/^[\x00-\xFF]{64,}$/smi", sid:1000003, rev:1);
